texts.exact_text: In (the condition denoted by) ䷮ Kùn there may (yet be) progress and success. For the firm and correct, the (really) great man, there will be good fortune. He will fall into no error. If he make speeches, his words cannot be made good.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 47; scan-backed transcription p. 161, hexagram statement

texts.exact_text: The first SIX, divided, shows its subject with bare buttocks straitened under the stump of a tree. He enters a dark valley, and for three years has no prospect (of deliverance).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 47; scan-backed transcription p. 161, line 1

texts.exact_text: The second NINE, undivided, shows its subject straitened amidst his wine and viands. There come to him anon the red knee-covers (of the ruler). It will be well for him (to maintain his sincerity as) in sacrificing. Active operations (on his part) will lead to evil, but he will be free from blame.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 47; scan-backed transcription p. 161, line 2

texts.exact_text: The third SIX, divided, shows its subject straitened before a (frowning) rock. He lays hold of thorns. He enters his palace, and does not see his wife. There will be evil.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 47; scan-backed transcription p. 161, line 3

texts.exact_text: The fourth NINE, undivided shows its subject proceeding very slowly (to help the subject of the first line), who is straitened by the carriage adorned with metal in front of him. There will be occasion for regret, but the end will be good.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 47; scan-backed transcription p. 161, line 4

texts.exact_text: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject with his nose and feet cut off. He is straitened by (his ministers in their) scarlet aprons. He is leisurely in his movements, however, and is satisfied. It will be well for him to be (as sincere) as in sacrificing (to spiritual beings).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 47; scan-backed transcription p. 161, line 5

texts.exact_text: The sixth SIX, divided, shows its subject straitened, as if bound with creepers; or n a high and dangerous position, and saying (to himself), 'If I move, I shall repent it.' If he do repent of former errors, there will be good fortune in his going forward.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 47; scan-backed transcription p. 161, line 6

texts.exact_text: 困，亨，貞，大人吉，无咎，有言不信。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 易經卦辭

texts.exact_text: 困，剛揜也。險以說，困而不失其所亨，其唯君子乎。貞大人吉，以剛中也；有言不信，尚口乃窮也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 彖

texts.exact_text: 澤无水，困。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 大象

texts.exact_text: 初六，臀困于株木，入于幽谷，三歲不覿。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 爻 1

texts.exact_text: 入于幽谷，幽不明也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 小象 1

texts.exact_text: 九二，困于酒食，朱紱方來，利用亨祀，征凶，无咎。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 爻 2

texts.exact_text: 困于酒食，中有慶也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 小象 2

texts.exact_text: 六三，困于石，據于蒺蔾。入于其宮，不見其妻，凶。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 爻 3

texts.exact_text: 據于蒺蔾，乘剛也。入于其宮，不見其妻，不祥也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 小象 3

texts.exact_text: 九四，來徐徐，困于金車，吝，有終。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 爻 4

texts.exact_text: 來徐徐，志在下也。雖不當位，有與也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 小象 4

texts.exact_text: 九五，劓刖，困于赤紱。乃徐有說，利用祭祀。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 爻 5

texts.exact_text: 劓刖，志未得也；乃徐有說，以中直也；利用祭祀，受福也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 小象 5

texts.exact_text: 上六，困于葛藟，于臲卼，曰動悔有悔，征吉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 爻 6

texts.exact_text: 困于葛藟，未當也；動悔有悔，吉行也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/困; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 47, 小象 6

texts.exact_text:
In ䷮ Kùn (we see) the strong (lines) covered and obscured (by the weak).

We have in it (the attribute of) perilousness going on to that of satisfaction. Who is it but the superior man that, though straitened, still does not fail in making progress to his proper end? For the firm and correct, the (really) great man, there will be good fortune:' -- this is shown by the central positions of the strong (lines). 'If he make speeches, his words cannot be made good:' -- to be fond of arguing or pleading is the way to be reduced to extremity.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix I, Hexagram 47, p. 253

texts.exact_text: (The trigram ☱ representing) a marsh, and (below it ☵ that for a defile, which has drained the other dry so that there is) no water in it, form ䷮ Kùn. The superior man, in accordance with this, will sacrifice his life in order to carry out his purpose.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 47, p. 326

texts.exact_text: 'He enters a dark valley:' -- so benighted is he, and without clear vision.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 47, line 1, p. 326

texts.exact_text: 'He is straitened amidst his wine and viands:' -- (but) his position is central, and there will be ground for congratulation.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 47, line 2, p. 326

texts.exact_text: 'He lays hold of thorns:' -- (this is suggested by the position of the line) above the strong (line).
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 47, line 3, p. 326

texts.exact_text: 'He proceeds very slowly (to help the subject of the first line):' -- his aim is directed to (help) that lower (line). Although he is not in his appropriate place, he and that other will (in the end) be together.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 47, line 4, p. 326

texts.exact_text: 'His nose and feet are cut off:' -- his aim has not yet been gained.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 47, line 5, p. 326

texts.exact_text: 'He is straitened as if bound with creepers: (his spirit and action) are unsuitable.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 47, line 6, p. 326
